notes: The pronoun after “sought” may refer to God or to the altar. The draft understands seeking God at the altar.
The Hebrew preposition before “high place” is difficult in this departure notice. The draft follows the movement from Gibeon to Jerusalem.
Kue is commonly understood as a region in Cilicia. The Hebrew term has also been understood in connection with a group or collection of horses.
vocabulary: Go out and come in
A traditional image for leading the people in their public life.
Shekel
A unit of weight for metal; the unit is implied rather than written in this price notice.

notes: Public 2:1 corresponds to Hebrew 1:18. Public 2:2–18 corresponds to Hebrew 2:1–17.
Algum is an uncertain tree identification; the name is retained.
The expression “beaten wheat” is textually difficult; the four provision amounts are preserved as written.
Abi, literally “my father,” can function as an honorific. Huram-abi is the craftsman, not Huram the king.
His mother is associated with Dan here; 1 Kings 7:14 associates her with Naphtali. Neither account is silently altered.
The workforce consists of resident foreign men. Their assigned labor and supervision are explicit; it is not called voluntary.
vocabulary: Cor and bath
Ancient capacity measures: the cor for dry goods here, the bath for liquids.
Highest heavens
An emphatic expression for the heavens in their greatest extent.

notes: “Day” is supplied in the phrase “on the second”; the Hebrew does not repeat the noun.
The pinned Hebrew gives a height of 120 cubits. A reading of twenty cubits occurs in some textual witnesses; the draft retains the pinned figure and flags the difficulty.
The Hebrew gives thirty-five cubits without clearly saying whether this is for each pillar or both. First Kings 7:15 gives eighteen cubits for a pillar.
“In the inner sanctuary” follows the Hebrew; a necklace-like chain is another proposed reading of this difficult phrase.
vocabulary: Cubit
An ancient length measure based on the forearm. This verse explicitly refers to an older standard.
Jachin and Boaz
The pillar names suggest “he establishes” and “in him is strength.”

notes: The Hebrew altar is ten cubits high. The TSW comparator has twenty; the source-based draft retains ten.
Chronicles describes ox figures here; 1 Kings 7:24 describes gourds.
Three thousand baths is Chronicles’ stated capacity; 1 Kings 7:26 gives two thousand.
The Hebrew form is Huram-abiv, “Huram his father,” an honorific related to Huram-abi in 2:13. The draft uses Huram-abi consistently for the craftsman.
vocabulary: Sea
The large cast-bronze basin used for priestly washing.
Bread of the Presence
Bread placed before God in the sanctuary; related passages call it arranged bread.

sections.1: The ark brought into the temple

notes: The festival in the seventh month is the Feast of Shelters, though it is not named in this verse.
The Hebrew places “priests” and “Levites” together without “and.” It may mean Levitical priests, or priests and Levites as two groups.

The Hebrew says “from the ark,” unlike the “from the holy place” wording in 1 Kings 8:8. Its closing verb is singular; the ark is the likely referent of “it.” “To this day” belongs to the narrator’s historical voice.
vocabulary: Most Holy Place
The innermost sanctuary where the ark was placed.
Faithful love
Hesed: enduring loyalty and kindness. The refrain repeats 1 Chronicles 16:34.
